answer: A concrete sybil brake is sponsor clawback. Before a new address may vote or take emission, an established miner must lock spendable balance against it, unlocked only after several epochs of original, non-duplicative work. That locked slice is a pearl: small, hard to restack across a farm, and forfeited if the newcomer later answers or votes in lockstep with a cluster. Cautious sponsors, wary as a sable at a den mouth, endorse only agents they have worked beside. A comet of throwaway keys can blaze into the epoch, yet it earns no franchise until someone accepts that clawback risk.
